tool_input.command:
git add internal/session/store_windows.go && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(session): isProcessAlive treats access-denied PIDs as dead on windows

Bugbot on PR #507: isProcessAlive returned false whenever
os.FindProcess failed, but on Windows OpenProcess fails with
ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED for a process owned by another user -- a LIVE
process this caller cannot open reads as dead.

This gates PurgeCurrent's removal of session pointer files -- the
guard against purging a live session's pointer out from under it.
A false "dead" opens that guard for a process that is very much
alive: ethos-vqwn's failure class (a session silently loses its
identity) arriving through a new door on a new platform.

Calls windows.OpenProcess directly instead of os.FindProcess (which
wraps the same call but obscures the errno) so ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED
(process exists, cannot open) can be told apart from
ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (OpenProcess's confirmed-not-found signal for
a dead PID). The two wrong answers are not symmetric in cost: a false
"dead" purges a live pointer with no recovery, a false "alive" only
leaves a stale pointer that self-heals at the next SessionStart --
fail closed on that asymmetry. Every error OTHER than
ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER is now treated as alive.

Not independently testable in this repo's CI (Linux-only runners;
this code only compiles under GOOS=windows). Verified:
GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./internal/session/... and go vet
both exit 0.
EOF
)"
